detailHeading: What goes into a bathroom that lasts
detailBody: Most bathroom problems start with water getting where it should not. Before new tile or a new vanity goes in, the subfloor, the wall behind the tub or shower, the shut-off valves and the exhaust fan are worth checking.

Georgian Bay homes and cottages see damp summers and cold winters. A fan that vents outside, a waterproof membrane behind shower tile and good caulking at every joint keep moisture out of the walls and help stop mould before it starts.

If you are planning ahead, mention how long you plan to stay in the home and who uses the bathroom. Blocking in the wall for a future grab bar, or a shower with a low curb, is simpler to add during a renovation than as a second job later.

faqs.q: Can my existing layout stay the same?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Many bathroom updates keep the toilet, sink and shower where they are, which keeps the work simpler. If you want to move a fixture, mention it in your request so the service provider can review the plumbing involved.
Pricing depends on the work, the materials and the condition of the space. The service provider reviews your request and talks through a quote before any work is approved.
Some plumbing and electrical work in Ontario must be done by a licensed contractor. The service provider can confirm what applies to your bathroom.

faqs.q: How is waterproofing handled in a shower?
faqs.a: Tiled showers go over a waterproof membrane before any tile is set. It is the part you never see, and the part that protects the walls and floor behind the tile.

faqs.q: Can I request work on a cottage bathroom?
faqs.a: Yes. Requests can cover homes and cottages. Mention if the property is seasonal, how to access it and any timing you need to plan around.
